newsitem.title: ITALY: Pope's appendix operation over-Italian agency.
newsitem.headline: Pope's appendix operation over-Italian agency.

text.p: Doctors completed surgery on Pope John Paul to remove his appendix on Tuesday, the Italian news agency ANSA said.

Quoting hospital sources, it said surgery on the 76-year-old Pope ended shortly before 9 a.m. (0700 GMT), less than two hours after he was taken into the operating theatre on the ninth floor of Rome's Gemelli hospital.
The ANSA report, which could not immediately be confirmed, did not say how the operation had gone or whether the Polish-born Pope had been moved back to his special 10th floor suite at the hospital.
A Gemelli spokesman said on Monday that a medical bulletin would be issued at around 11 a.m. (0900 GMT).
The Vatican announced plans for surgery last month in a statement which said a recurrent inflammation of the appendix was the cause of three bouts of fever the Pope has suffered since Christmas.

Tuesday's operation was the Pope's fifth in 15 years. He had major abdominal surgery twice in 1981 after being shot in an assassination attempt and in 1992 to remove a colon tumour. The Pope underwent hip replacement surgery in 1994.
